Welcome everyone. Point to the bus: Lessons 1 to 6 are ticked. Today the bus moves on to Lesson 7: Santa catches the bus. This is the first of the two Christmas lessons. The first part of this deck looks back at Lesson 6, then the whole term, then it introduces Lesson 7 before students get the worksheet. Allow about 30 to 40 minutes.

Remember Lesson 6?

What does it mean? Tell your partner. Then click.
In Lesson 6 we peeked at the silly season. Today it really starts!
Term 4  ·  Explore community services
Quick recall of the four silly season words from the end of Lesson 6. Pairs say the meaning first, then click a card. Challenge: ask your partner "What are you doing on Boxing Day?" All four words come up again today.

Talk about the term

Ask your partner. Answer, then add more.
1
How do you usually get to class?
2
Which place have you visited this term?
3
What did you do last weekend?
4
What are you going to do in the holidays?
Example: I usually catch the bus. It's handy. It stops right outside.
Term 4  ·  Explore community services
Pairs, about 5 minutes. A short version of the Lesson 6 term chat, with four of the five tenses: simple present, present perfect, past simple and be going to. Push "answer, then add more": a short answer plus one or two details. Ask two or three students to tell the class about their partner.

Term 4  ·  Explore community services
Make the link clear. Lesson 6 put the whole term together and ended with a peek at December. Lesson 7 is the first full Christmas lesson: Santa is new in Sydney, and the students are his helpers. It revises Lessons 1 and 4 and adds eight new expressions for the silly season. Next is Lesson 8, Christmas lunch for eighty.

Lesson 7: your route

Today we start at stop 1
Stop 1Talk first: Julia and Alan talk about Santa catching the bus.
Term 4  ·  Explore community services
Walk the route with the class. Click a stop to show what it is about. Lesson 7 has 10 stops and 31 activities: talk first (listening), 16 expressions (eight old, eight new), Say it, grammar (now or always, and comparing), envelopes and councils, the Crows Nest map, Opal cards and a timetable, the sleigh or the ferry debate, two games (Santa's run and backyard cricket) and check your learning. There is lots of standing up and moving today.

Which lesson was it?

What does it mean? Which lesson? Guess, then click.
Two more to remember: I reckon, it's a pain. Listen for all eight today!
Term 4  ·  Explore community services
Pairs say the meaning and guess the lesson, then click. One point for the meaning, one point for the lesson. Ask for the meaning of the last two (I reckon = I think; it's a pain = it's annoying). These are the eight in Set 1 of Stop 2 (Activity 5). All eight are in the Julia and Alan conversation.

Pairs match each technique to its lesson, then click Show. Read the examples aloud and ask: which technique is it? (The first two keep it going with a question, the last two point and explain.) In Activity 3, students find three of each in the Julia and Alan conversation, then play "Keep it going" in groups of four.

Now or always?

Say the verb with your partner first. Then click the blank.
1
Look! The elves (wrap) the presents now.
2
Santa (come) every year.
3
The ferry (leave) every 30 minutes.
4
Julia (buy) a green hat at the moment.
Always: simple present (facts, habits, timetables).  Now: present continuous (am / is / are + verb-ing).
Term 4  ·  Explore community services
Pairs say each sentence first, then click the blanks. Ask: which time words helped? (Look! now, every year, every 30 minutes, at the moment.) Stop 4 of the worksheet has the full grammar box, then in / on / at, and comparing (cheaper, the fastest, it takes). Keep this short.

Term 4  ·  Explore community services
Quick Lesson 4 recall. Pairs choose, then click Show: the Gold Senior/Pensioner card. Then ask who each card is for: Adult (most people), Child/Youth (4 to 15), Concession (some students and other eligible people), Gold (NSW Seniors Card holders and eligible pensioners), bank card or phone (adult fare). In Activity 24, students choose for Mrs Claus, the elves and a baby reindeer.
